Title: Regex Bypass in Redirect Validation leading to Path Traversal and Open Redirect
Analysis:
### Vulnerability Analysis:
The function `RedirectUtils.verifyRedirectUri` verifies if the user-supplied `redirect_uri` matches any configured redirect URIs for the client, including wildcard configurations such as `https://example.com/test/*`. To prevent path traversal attacks (e.g., using `..` to traverse out of the allowed path), it runs a regex check via `areWildcardsAllowed(URI)` using the pattern `UNSAFE_PATH_PATTERN`:

```java
private final static Pattern UNSAFE_PATH_PATTERN = Pattern.compile(
        "(/|%2[fF]|%5[cC]|\\\\\\\\)(%2[eE]|\\\\.){2}(/|%2[fF]|%5[cC]|\\\\\\\\)|(/|%2[fF]|%5[cC]|\\\\\\\\)(%2[eE]|\\\\.){2}$");
```

This pattern checks for directory traversal sequences like `/../` or `/..` at the end of the string. However, it assumes that the characters immediately following `..` must be either a directory separator (`/`, `\`, `%2F`, `%5C`) or the end of the string (`$`).

By appending a path parameter delimiter `;` immediately after the two dots (e.g., `..;`), an attacker can bypass this check. For instance, the URL `https://example.com/test/..;foo/bar` is recognized as a valid wildcard match under `https://example.com/test/*` because:
1. `areWildcardsAllowed` returns `true` since the sequence `/..;` does not match the trailing separator requirement of `UNSAFE_PATH_PATTERN`.
2. `matchesRedirects` successfully validates that the URL starts with `https://example.com/test/`.

When the user is redirected to `https://example.com/test/..;foo/bar`, standard servlet containers (such as Tomcat) and reverse proxies parse path parameters starting with `;` and strip them before resolving relative paths. Thus, the backend container resolves `..;foo` to `..` (parent directory) and normalizes the path to `https://example.com/bar`, allowing directory traversal and open redirection outside the configured whitelist boundaries.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
An attacker can initiate an authentication request with the following parameters:

```http
GET /realms/myrealm/protocol/openid-connect/auth?client_id=myclient&response_type=code&redirect_uri=https://example.com/test/..;foo/bar HTTP/1.1
Host: keycloak.local
```

Keycloak will validate `https://example.com/test/..;foo/bar` against the allowed pattern `https://example.com/test/*`, successfully bypass the `UNSAFE_PATH_PATTERN` check, and issue an HTTP 302 redirect:

```http
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Location: https://example.com/test/..;foo/bar
```

When parsed by the browser or the target server (e.g., behind Tomcat), the path resolves to `https://example.com/bar` instead of a subdirectory under `/test/`.

Title: Arbitrary File Read / Path Traversal in /consoles/*filepath Endpoint
Analysis:
In `web/web.go`, the endpoint `/consoles/*filepath` is registered and maps to `(h *Handler) consoles(w, r)`. In `consoles`, the route parameter `filepath` is fetched via `route.Param(ctx, \"filepath\")` into `name` (e.g. `127.0.0.1:9090/consoles/../../../../etc/passwd`). This parameter `name` is then opened via `http.Dir(h.options.ConsoleTemplatesPath).Open(name)`. Because `http.Dir` under the hood uses `filepath.Join` or similar standard file operations, but when accessed via its `Open` method directly, it does not fully restrict directory traversal if the parameter contains relative path segments like `../` and the HTTP server does not sanitize it (especially since it's matched using `*filepath` wildcard router param which preserves slashes). 

More importantly, the content of the file is loaded into memory, parsed as a Go template, and expanded via `ExpandHTML`. If a file is successfully parsed (or if it contains template tags or is just treated as raw template text), the expander will process it. 

Furthermore, `http.Dir.Open` allows a Directory Traversal / Path Traversal vulnerability that allows an attacker to read arbitrary files from the filesystem (or attempt to render them as templates, which can leak secrets or source files) if they have access to the Prometheus server.

### Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A GET request to:
`GET /consoles/../../../../etc/passwd HTTP/1.1`

This bypasses any routing restrictions due to the `*filepath` wildcard, retrieving the arbitrary file `/etc/passwd`.
